alternative_explanations: Stable error-correcting task descriptors may reduce learned routing to a classical dictionary or nearest-code index; any K-independent result could come entirely from supplied identity structure.
The finite transformation hypothesis library may perform the essential induction, making expert specialization a compact program lookup rather than learned neural modularity.
Dense shared random features may underfit discrete byte operations; direct program and dense expert sweep are therefore the stronger matched exact controls.
confounds: The plan intentionally tests the interaction of heterogeneous learned transformations and feature-based routing because EXP-0006 already isolated homogeneous sharding; it cannot attribute a failure to one component without a child experiment.
Only six experts are active in scored tasks while all K experts are trained, so the test isolates dormant capacity but not open-world arrival of unseen skills or accelerator communication.
falsification_criteria: Reduce HYP-0010 if learned_sparse_modules has accuracy, held-out composition or routing accuracy below 0.95 in any cell, activates other than exactly D modules, or gains apparent efficiency by omitting descriptor encoding, router lookup, expert bytes, fit, state or update work.

Treat separate sparse modules as null and make HYP-0010 dormant if direct_program_index matches learned_sparse_modules capability and is no worse on exact mean query operations, bytes loaded, persistent state, fit operations and update operations; nomenclature or object containers are not an architectural gain.
Reject a fixed-sparsity scaling claim if dense_expert_sweep or learned sparse query work, bytes loaded or routing error grows materially with dormant K at fixed active sequence and D.

outcome_policy.negative: If learned routing or held-out composition fails, lower HYP-0010 and stop tuning this modular toy; preserve whether the failure came from routing, expert induction or dense interference and pivot to another family.
outcome_policy.null: If learned sparse composes exactly but direct program matches or dominates it, lower HYP-0010 and retain sparse modules only as a known conditional-computation implementation, not a distinct successor principle.
outcome_policy.positive: Keep HYP-0010 testing only if learned sparse is exact, K-independent end to end, activates exactly D modules and beats both direct program and dense shared controls on at least one exact capability-cost axis without losing another; then preregister an adversarial multi-seed screen.

predicted_outcome: Training shows each of K functionally heterogeneous byte transformations only as single-step demonstrations under a stable random 16-bit descriptor; scored queries use held-out one-bit descriptor variants, unseen inputs and compositions of D primitives drawn from a fixed six-module active set while K adds trained but dormant experts. Random routing and primitive memorization exact accuracy are at most 0.10. Learned sparse modules, flat direct program, dense expert sweep and oracle are predicted to reach accuracy, held-out composition and routing accuracy at least 0.95 in every cell. Learned sparse activates exactly D modules and, like direct program and oracle, uses a radius-one index with near-zero K query slope; dense sweep is exact but has approximately linear router, bytes and full-expert evaluations in K. The flat direct program is expected to match learned sparse capability while using no more operations, bytes, state, fit or update work, yielding a registered null for separate module containers. Dense shared random features may retain partial composition but are predicted below 0.90 average accuracy.
promotion_criteria: Quick cannot promote HYP-0010. A later screen is justified only if learned sparse passes every exact capability and accounting gate, is non-dominated by direct program, dense shared, dense sweep and oracle controls, survives confusable descriptors without a supplied route ID, and acknowledges SRC-0004, SRC-0015 through SRC-0017 and SRC-0035 through SRC-0038.
research_question: Can a learned sparse router identify and compose reusable heterogeneous transformations from opaque task demonstrations with full query work independent of growing dormant-expert count K, and does representing those transformations as separate modules provide any exact capability-cost advantage over a flat learned direct program using the identical router?
title: Held-out composition of learned heterogeneous modules versus a flat direct program
